title: Cloud Administration Command
summary: Cloud administration command uses the management plane of a cloud provider to run code inside virtual machines, bypassing the need for a network path or a working login on the guest itself. Services such as AWS Systems Manager Run Command, Azure Run Command, and automation runbooks rely on an agent installed in the machine, and the provider delivers the script to that agent over the agent's existing outbound connection. Anyone holding sufficient permissions in the cloud subscription, including a delegated administrator account, can therefore execute commands across many machines at once. From a defender's perspective the execution appears in the cloud audit log rather than in the guest operating system, so host logs may show a process whose parent is the management agent and no interactive session at all. Detection pairs the provider audit event with the process creation it produced inside the guest, and looks for commands issued by identities or from addresses that do not match normal administration.

beginner.definition: Cloud platforms offer a way to run commands on virtual machines without logging in to them directly. An agent inside the machine receives the instruction and runs it. If an attacker takes over that cloud feature, they can run commands on many machines at once.
beginner.whyItMatters: This route needs no open network port and no working password on the machine. One permission mistake in the cloud account can mean control of every machine in the subscription. Host based tools may notice nothing unusual, because the command arrives through a trusted agent. It also scales, so damage can spread quickly across a whole environment. Watching who uses these features matters as much as watching the machines.
howItWorks: Each virtual machine in the cloud runs a management agent that talks to the provider.
An administrator, or an attacker with the right cloud permissions, prepares a script.
They call the management service and name the machines that should receive the script.
The provider passes the script to each agent through the existing outbound connection.
The agent runs the script on the machine, usually with high system privileges.
Results return through the cloud service, and the whole action is recorded in the audit log.
beginner.example: Picture a large hotel where every room has a small speaker. The front desk can send a spoken instruction to any room. The room speaker then repeats it to the cleaner inside. Nobody from outside ever walks along the corridors. Now imagine someone sits at the front desk with a stolen staff card. They speak into the microphone and tell cleaners in fifty rooms to leave the doors unlocked. The cleaners hand over the keys. The corridors stay quiet and no guest sees a stranger. Cloud administration command is that microphone, and the stolen card is the cloud permission.
takeaways: Cloud management tools are a command channel into your virtual machines.
Protect the permissions that allow remote command execution, and log every use.
Correlate cloud audit events with process creation inside the guest machine.

objectives: Explain how a cloud management service can run code inside a virtual machine.
Describe why this path bypasses normal network and guest login controls.
Identify the cloud audit events that record remote command execution.
Explain how a delegated administrator account widens the reach of the technique.
List the conditions that make a cloud issued command look abnormal.
